Records also have 'pages': the in-world text shown when you read the object (kind 'record' in a map). Monster entries come from bestiary.json; chapter entries from chapters.json.

creation.title: The Null and the Five Axioms

parts.text: Before the beginning there was the Null: not emptiness, but something undefined. Nothing could be counted, so nothing could exist.
Five Axioms woke: 'There is one.' 'One can follow one.' 'Equal things stay equal.' 'Between two points, a line.' 'What changes, changes by a rule.' Where they held, Mathea became real.
Mathematical Energy - the force that 'holds' wherever an Axiom is true. Counting, balance, form and change all run on it.
When the Numera is disturbed, patterns stutter: numbers drift in the air, structures wake and MathMon turn wild.
Five rivers of Numera run beneath Mathea. Each region sits on one: the Root of Counting (Number Forest), Balance (Algebra Cavern), Form (Geometry Kingdom) and Change (Chronos Dimension).
The First Axiom, 'There is one', shattered into light when the world began. Its shards became the Crystal Realm.
All five Roots cross at one place: the Zero Point, where every count begins.
Where Numera pooled, it began to repeat itself. A pattern that learned to keep its shape became alive: the first MathMon.
Young MathMon imitate the animals they see. Ancient ones stop imitating and become stranger - living symbols, shapes and light.
A MathMon's pattern is steadied by understanding. When its trainer truly works something out, that clarity flows into the partner and its move lands true. Guessing makes the pattern wobble.
The Tallyfolk (forest), the Order of the Unknown (caverns), Euclidia the Kingdom of Form, and the Timekeepers of Chronos. All faded about a thousand years ago.
The Professor says they faded through natural Numera decay.
Euclidia's chronicle says otherwise: they faded because of something they did together.
The first people to befriend MathMon - by counting with them. One stone, one MathMon, one friend.
They raised the Arch of Sums and the first Numera Seals.
Scholars of the Algebra Cavern who learned that an 'x' is a promise: a value exists even before you know it. They stored Numera inside equations.
Their charter forbade 'any reckoning of the whole'. Someone broke that rule.
Architects who shaped Numera into buildings that could never fall, as long as every angle was exact.
Their last builders wrote that the Unravelling 'came from our own hands'.
Measurers of the Root of Change, keepers of the Great Clock that sequences Mathea's days.
Twenty years ago their last village froze at 3:14.
Stone seals in every region, each guarded by a powerful MathMon. The old songs say they hold 'what remains'.
They were not failing. They were being opened.
The Seal of Sums bore new tool marks and wet ink: someone had opened it recently.
A word carved on the Tallyfolk stones and spoken by the hooded stranger. The corruption has a name.
The Remainder is Numera that fits no pattern - left over when the ancients' great calculation 'did not come out even'.
It is not an error. In division, what is left over is where the next count begins. The Remainder is what lets anything new happen.
The four civilisations tried to compute the Final Number: the exact total of all Numera, so nothing could ever be uncertain again.
The calculation left a Remainder, and the world unravelled.
The Origin Engine was built to run it.
'The Engine', the stranger called it. Something the Professor 'will know'.
A machine at the Zero Point built by all four civilisations to perform the Last Calculation.
Twenty years ago, two researchers restarted it.
Beneath the Time Spire, where all five Axiom Roots cross. The Origin Engine waits there.
Two researchers, 'N.' and 'V.', reopened the Order's Remainder vault.
They restarted the Origin Engine to cure the fading Numera. One step was never checked. The Engine misfired and a Timekeeper village froze at 3:14.
N. told the council it was 'natural decay'.
The hooded stranger draws the Remainder out of each freed guardian into a glass phial. She is gathering it all - on purpose.
A pocket communicator built by Professor Numeris. Text only - 'I'm hopeless with gadgets that talk.'
You sealed the Origin Engine forever. Vera left alone.
You and the Professor persuaded Vera to stop. A clock in Chronos moved to 3:15.
The Remainder Theorem: what remains is where the next count begins. Vera's village woke at dawn.
Starter Village's MathMon researcher and your mentor. Brilliant, curious, forgetful (his glasses are usually on his head). Motto: 'Mistakes are just data!'
His research notes jump from 'Year 0' to 'Year 20'. The pages in between are missing.
A burnt log in the Dragon Keep is in his handwriting: 'I told the council it was natural decay.'
He skipped one check twenty years ago, and hid it. He became a teacher so no student of his would ever skip one.
His journal: 'Every day I tell them mistakes are data. Every day I hide mine.'
A Timekeeper girl who once ran between the clock towers of Chronos with her sums.
The hooded stranger. The Professor's former research partner. She wears a pocket watch stopped at 3:14 and wants to finish the Last Calculation so nothing can go wrong again.
She now guest-lectures in the Professor's class 'How To Check Your Work'.
Watched you free the Arithmetic Beast. 'That's one.'
Collects the Remainder from each guardian.
Revealed: Vera Tallow.
Your rival. Loud, fast, and secretly practises his times tables every night.
The village historian. Gets dates slightly wrong on purpose to see if you notice.
A village kid whose DIVOWL, Sums, flew away when the Counting Stone flickered.
A nervous, honest scientist of the Algebra Cavern. Twenty years ago she assisted two visiting researchers.
Knight of Euclidia's last line. Formal, kind, and very fond of right angles.
The last Timekeeper still moving in time. He knew Vera as a child.
Starter Village: whitewashed houses, the Counting Stone, the Mathmart, the Sanctuary, the Recovery Center and the Professor's lab.
Green Meadow: grass grows in counting spirals. Tallyfolk tally stones stand among the flowers.
Ancient Number Ruins: fallen counting arches and three Numera Seals around the Arch of Sums.
Beyond: Pine Ridge, Waterfall Plateau, the Sunsand Desert, Mirror Beach and the farms - the Root of Counting runs under all of it.
Floating islands of light where the First Axiom shattered. The Prism Archive keeps the oldest record of all.
Crystals grow in balanced pairs; unsolved equations glow on the walls.
The Glow Tunnels and Echo Hollow, where equations echo back half-finished.
The Lost Laboratory of the Order of the Unknown, with its Remainder vault.
Euclidia: dead-straight roads, obelisks with exact shadows, hedges at perfect right angles.
The Garden and Pillar Courts, measured to the finger-width.
The Dragon Keep, folded into impossible shapes.
Islands hang still in the air. Every clock shows 3:14.
The Tick and Tock Isles - the frozen Timekeeper village.
The Time Spire, and beneath it the Zero Point.

record_counting_stone.title: The Counting Stone
pages: The village Counting Stone. Its carvings read: 'ONE, AND ONE MORE, AND ONE MORE. WE COUNT TOGETHER SO NOTHING IS FORGOTTEN.'
Below, newer marks: someone has scratched a tiny 'r' next to the last number. You can't tell how old it is.

parts.text: 'We count together so nothing is forgotten.' Someone scratched an 'r' beside the last number.

record_tally_stones.title: Tallyfolk Tally Stones
pages: Rows of tally marks, grouped in fives. Beside them, carved figures of people and MathMon counting side by side.
'WE BUILT THE ARCH OF SUMS SO THE COUNT WOULD ALWAYS BALANCE. WHAT REMAINS, WE SEALED.'

parts.text: 'We built the Arch of Sums so the count would always balance. What remains, we sealed.'

record_arch_inscription.title: Inscription on the Arch of Sums
pages: 'THE FOUR PEOPLES MET AT THE ZERO POINT TO RECKON THE WHOLE OF THE WORLD.'
'THE COUNT DID NOT COME OUT EVEN. WHAT REMAINED BROKE LOOSE, AND THE WORLD UNRAVELLED.'
'NEVER COMPLETE THE CALCULATION.'

parts.text: 'The count did not come out even. What remained broke loose, and the world unravelled. Never complete the calculation.'

record_professor_notes.title: The Professor's Research Notes
pages: Neat notebooks on the lab shelf: 'Numera Flow, Year 0', 'Remainder Theory (with V.), Year 0'...
...and then 'Teaching Notes, Year 20'. Nothing in between. Twenty years of research are simply missing.

parts.text: 'Remainder Theory (with V.), Year 0' - then nothing until 'Teaching Notes, Year 20'.

record_journal.title: The Professor's Journal
pages: 'Year 0, the night after. The Engine misfired because I didn't check the carry in step nine. I was sure. I was proud.'
'I told the council it was natural decay. Vera knows. She hasn't spoken to me since.'
'Every day I tell my students mistakes are data. Every day I hide mine. If anyone ever reads this: I'm sorry.'
Tucked inside: a copy of the ancients' last record. 'What remains is where the next count begins. Keep it.'

parts.text: 'Every day I tell my students mistakes are data. Every day I hide mine.' With it, a copy of the ancients' last record.

record_prism_archive.title: The Prism Archive
pages: Light bends through the crystal into words: 'THERE IS ONE.'
'AND WHEN ONE SHATTERS, THERE ARE MANY. NOTHING IS LOST THAT IS ONLY DIVIDED.'

parts.text: 'Nothing is lost that is only divided.'

record_order_charter.title: Charter of the Order of the Unknown
pages: 'ARTICLE ONE: EVERY UNKNOWN IS A PROMISE. KEEP YOUR PROMISES.'
'ARTICLE NINE: NO MEMBER SHALL ATTEMPT A RECKONING OF THE WHOLE.' Someone has underlined it three times.

parts.text: 'No member shall attempt a reckoning of the whole.' Underlined three times.

record_vault_log.title: Remainder Vault Log
pages: 'Vault sealed, year of the Unravelling. Contents: Remainder, one part in nine.'
A newer line in different ink: 'Vault opened for study. Year 0. Two visitors.'

parts.text: 'Vault opened for study. Year 0. Two visitors.'

record_vexa_notes.title: Dr. Vexa's Old Notes
pages: 'Assisted N. and V. today. Brilliant pair. V. checks everything twice. N. checks nothing he's sure of.'
'They want to carry the vault's Remainder to the Zero Point. I don't like it. They say it will cure the fading Numera.'

parts.text: 'V. checks everything twice. N. checks nothing he's sure of.'

record_euclid_chronicle.title: The Euclidian Chronicle
pages: 'Our kingdom did not fall to decay, whatever later scholars may claim.'
'We joined the Last Calculation. When it failed, our angles stopped adding to one hundred and eighty, and our towers folded.'

parts.text: 'Our kingdom did not fall to decay, whatever later scholars may claim.'

record_builders_last.title: The Last Builder's Note
pages: 'The dragon that guards our keep was a friend once. We folded it to hold the Remainder. Forgive us, Dimensia.'
'The Unravelling came from our own hands.'

parts.text: 'The Unravelling came from our own hands.'

record_burnt_log.title: A Burnt Log Page
pages: Half a page, scorched at the edges, in looping handwriting:
'...Engine misfire, Year 0. Chronos village frozen. I told the council it was natural decay. I could not say it was me. - A.N.'

parts.text: 'I told the council it was natural decay. I could not say it was me. - A.N.'

record_great_clock.title: Face of the Great Clock
pages: 'WHAT CHANGES, CHANGES BY A RULE. KEEP THE RULE, AND TIME KEEPS YOU.'
The clock's hands are stopped at 3:14. Its pendulum hangs mid-swing.

parts.text: 'Keep the rule, and time keeps you.' Stopped at 3:14.

record_frozen_village.title: Register of the Tock Isles
pages: A village register, open on its last page. Names, and the time each family last signed in.
'TALLOW: Lina (mother), Teo (son). 3:14.' A third line has been added in fresher ink: 'Vera (daughter): away at the Engine.'

parts.text: 'Tallow: Lina (mother), Teo (son). 3:14. Vera (daughter): away at the Engine.'

record_engine_plan.title: Plan of the Origin Engine
pages: A carved diagram: five roots meeting in a circle at the Zero Point. Around it, the Engine - a calculation in stone, nine steps long.
At the bottom, in four different scripts: 'IF IT DOES NOT COME OUT EVEN, STOP.'

parts.text: A nine-step calculation in stone. 'If it does not come out even, stop.'
